THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 -3-  NC: 2023:KHC:43161  MFA No. 3871 of 2019  JUDGMENT
This is an appeal filed by the claimants aggrieved by the award passed in MVC No.646/2018, dated 27.02.2019 by the Court of Principal Senior Civil Judge & Additional MACT-III, Chitradurga.

entities.text: Principal Senior Civil Judge & Additional MACT-III, Chitradurga
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The claim petition is filed claiming compensation of an amount of Rs.40,00,000/- for the death of the deceased in a road traffic accident.
The claimants are the husband, sons and two married daughters, told four claimants.
It is the case of the claimants that the deceased was working as a Mason and also doing milk vending business and earning an amount of Rs.20,000/- p.m.
As there was no evidence placed in this regard the court below had taken an amount of Rs.8,000/- p.m.
The claimed compensation is Rs.40,00,000/- and the court below has awarded compensation of an amount of Rs.5,18,000/-.

sentences.text:
The court below while computing the compensation has observed that as none of the claimants are dependants on the income of the deceased they are only entitled for 'loss of estate' savings but not under the head of 'loss of dependency' and considering the income at Rs.8,000/- under the head 'loss of estate/savings' the court below granted an amount of Rs.4,48,000/-, towards loss of consortium an amount of Rs.40,000/- was awarded, towards loss of estate an amount of Rs.15,000/- was awarded, towards transportation and funeral expenses an amount of Rs.15,000/-
was granted.
Altogether an amount of Rs.5,18,000/- was awarded by the court below.
4. Learned counsel for the claimants submits that it is the case of the husband that the family and the children were depending on the income of the deceased.
This aspect was not considered by the Tribunal and granted compensation only under the head of loss of estate.

It is submitted that with regard to the income the NC: 2023:KHC:43161 court below had taken the income of the deceased at Rs.8,000/-, when it is the case of the claimants that the deceased was earning Rs.20,000/-.
The compensation that was granted under other heads also was not just and reasonable.

5. Learned counsel for the insurance company submits that at any stretch of imagination the claimants cannot be termed as dependants and in the light of the law laid down by this court in A.
Manavalagan vs A. Krishnamurthy And Others1, the claimants are not entitled for loss of dependency and the court below had rightly considered the same and no grounds are made out for enhancement of the compensation.

A.
Manavalagan vs A. Krishnamurthy And Others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:

6. Having heard the learned counsel on either side, perused the entire material on record.
In this case first coming to the income.
According to the claimants the deceased was earning an amount of Rs.20,000/- p.m., the court below had granted an amount of Rs.8,000/-.
This is ILR 2004 KAR 3268 NC: 2023:KHC:43161 court below had granted an amount of Rs.8,000/-.
This is an accident of the year 2017.
Hence, this court is inclined to take the monthly income of the deceased as Rs.11,000/-.

As the deceased was 45 years old future prospects has to be considered at 25% i.e.,
2,950/- (11,000 + 2,950)= 13,950/- .Now
the issue is about the dependency.
No doubt the claimants are major son, two married daughters and husband.
The court below had rightly held that they are not dependants.
When it comes to the husband it is his case that he was depending on the income of the wife, as far as the husband is concerned this court is inclined to consider the husband as dependant.
As he is the only person depending, out of Rs.13,750/-, 50% has to be deducted towards personal expenses, then the contribution to the family is Rs.6,875/-.
Hence, the claimants are entitled for an amount of Rs.11,55,000/- (6,875 x 12 x 14) towards loss of dependency.
Towards consortium an amount of Rs.1,76,000/- (Rs.44,000 x 4), towards funeral expenses an amount of Rs.33,000/- is awarded.

In the light of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of V.MEKALA vs. M.
MALATHI AND ANOTHER2, the claimant is entitled for an amount of Rs.10,000/- towards Legal Manjunatha vs S L L Kantha on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192748464/

8. The claimant is therefore, entitled to the compensation under the following heads:
 Heads Compensation  Awarded  1. Loss of Dependency : Rs. 11,55,000/-
 2. Loss of Consortium : Rs. 1,76,000/-
 3. Funeral Expenses : Rs. 33,000/-
 4. Legal Expenses : Rs. 10,000/-
Accordingly, the appeal is partly allowed, enhancing the compensation amount from Rs.5,18,000/- to Rs.13,74,000/-.
i) The enhanced amount shall carry interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of realization.
ii) The respondent - insurance company shall deposit the amount within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of copy of the judgment.
On such deposit, the claimant is entitled to withdraw the entire amount without furnishing any security.
iii) Registry is directed to return the Trial Court Records to the Tribunal, along with certified copy of the order passed by this Court forthwith without any delay.

iv) No costs.
 NC: 2023:KHC:43161 Pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.
